answer_text:
Let \(\sigma\) be the nontrivial automorphism of \(L/\mathbb{Q}\), so

\[
\sigma(\sqrt{-11})=-\sqrt{-11}.
\]

If \(x,y\in\mathbb{Q}\), then

\[
\sigma(x+y\sqrt{-11})=x-y\sqrt{-11}.
\]

Therefore the field norm is

\[
N_{L/\mathbb{Q}}(x+y\sqrt{-11})
=(x+y\sqrt{-11})(x-y\sqrt{-11})
=x^2+11y^2.
\]

So the formula is correct for elements of the form \(x+y\sqrt{-11}\) with rational coefficients, in particular for integer \(x,y\).

However, the ring of integers is larger than \(\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{-11}]\). A general element of \(\mathcal{O}_L\) is

\[
a+b\omega,\qquad \omega=\frac{1+\sqrt{-11}}{2},
\]

and its norm is

\[
N_{L/\mathbb{Q}}(a+b\omega)=a^2+ab+3b^2.
\]

Equivalently, if one writes an algebraic integer as \(\frac{u+v\sqrt{-11}}{2}\) with \(u\equiv v\pmod 2\), then

\[
N\left(\frac{u+v\sqrt{-11}}{2}\right)=\frac{u^2+11v^2}{4}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\text{Yes, }N(x+y\sqrt{-11})=x^2+11y^2\text{ for }x,y\in\mathbb{Q};\text{ for general }\mathcal{O}_L,\ N(a+b\omega)=a^2+ab+3b^2.}
\]
